meta.title: How to use Research Notebook
meta.subtitle: A complete walkthrough of the desktop app: install, write, capture evidence from PDFs, record audio, search, export, back up and recover.
meta.note: This guide describes the current 0.1.0 build, including its limits. Where a feature is not available, it says so.

sections.title: Install and launch
sections.intro: Get the 0.1.0 package for your operating system (x64). Keep a separate copy of important research before testing. There is no automatic updater in this build.

groups.heading: Windows
steps: Installed copy: run Research-Notebook-0.1.0-Setup-x64.exe. It is a one-click, per-user installer.
Portable copy: run Research-Notebook-0.1.0-Portable-x64.exe. Portable describes how the executable launches; your library is not stored beside it.
The packages are unsigned. If Windows shows a trust prompt, check that you obtained the expected package first.

groups.heading: Linux
steps: AppImage: make the file executable (chmod +x Research-Notebook-0.1.0-linux-x64.AppImage) and open it.
DEB: sudo apt install ./Research-Notebook-0.1.0-linux-x64.deb
RPM (Fedora): sudo dnf install ./Research-Notebook-0.1.0-linux-x64.rpm
Open Research Notebook from your application launcher after installing a DEB or RPM.

sections.expected: An empty workspace, or your existing local library, opens. If launch fails, record the exact message and package filename. Do not repeatedly reinstall over your only copy of a library.

sections.title: How your data is stored
sections.intro: A notebook holds a research project. A page groups a topic. A note is a small document on a page. A block is one piece of a note: evidence, interpretation, a question or media.
bullets: Everything is saved to a local SQLite database plus managed asset folders.
See Application menu → settings → Library & Storage → Active library for the real location.
Default location: %APPDATA%\research-notebook on Windows, ~/.config/research-notebook on Linux.
There is no cloud sync or sign-in. OpenRouter transcription is a separate, optional network action.
Text and titles save when you leave their field. Click elsewhere before changing pages or closing the app.
Keep the database and assets together when recovering a library.

sections.title: Create notebooks, pages and notes
steps: Select Create notebook (empty library) or New notebook at the bottom of the sidebar. The app creates Untitled notebook and its first Untitled page.
Click the notebook title in the sidebar, type a name, then click elsewhere to save.
Click Page title at the top of the workspace, type a name, then click elsewhere. The sidebar label updates.
Type a name in New page and press Enter, or use the small Create page icon.
Select Add note (or Create first note on an empty page). Use Add note again for more notes.
sections.expected: Each note shows Add block, Record audio and the command-menu button. Notes have no visible title, rename or delete command in this build.

subsections.heading: Select the receiving note and load longer pages
steps: Click into a text block or focus a control inside the note you want. Its document gets a focus outline; clicking blank background is not reliable.
Focus the note again before each PDF capture or attachment. Reloading the workspace clears the active-note selection, and Research capture then uses the first note.
On pages with more than 50 notes, scroll to Load more notes. Each click adds the next batch.

sections.title: Write and save semantic blocks
sections.intro: Choose Write for the full-width editor. Select Add block for a plain text block, or open the block command menu (the Type / for commands button) for another type. Type, then click elsewhere to save. There is no Save button.
bullets: All seven types use the same plain text editor. They label purpose; they do not evaluate or answer anything.
A manually inserted source text or quote does not gain PDF provenance. Use PDF capture for a source link.
Typing / in a text block does not open the menu in this build. Click the Type / for commands button.
The /audio menu entry only shows guidance. Use Record audio to record.
There is no rich-text toolbar, code, table or divider insertion.

subsections.heading: Duplicate, move, answer or delete a block
steps: Hover a block and click its three-dot Actions for … block button.
Duplicate appends a copy to the same note. Check its position.
Move up / Move down shifts one place; the command is disabled at the start or end.
On a question, Add answer appends a blank answer linked by responds to.
Move to trash removes a block recoverably (see Trash).

subsections.heading: Reorder with mouse or keyboard
steps: Drag the dotted handle onto another block in the same note. Upper half drops before, lower half drops after.
Or focus a text block and press Alt + ↑ or Alt + ↓.
Reordering works within one note only, not between notes or pages.

subsections.heading: Convert blocks, link reasoning, inspect metadata
steps: Open Actions → Inspector. Use Convert block to switch between the seven text types. Text is preserved; media blocks cannot be converted.
Choose a Relation type: explains, responds to, comments on or summarizes. Direction runs from the inspected block to the target.
Pick a target in Block to link and select Link. Targets are other blocks in the loaded notes of this page.
Use the small cross on a relation row to remove it. This does not delete either block.
Metadata is read-only JSON. For sourced blocks, View source provenance jumps to the source.
Select Close inspector when done.

sections.title: Read PDFs and capture evidence
sections.intro: PDF import copies the file into the notebook's managed assets. Use a PDF without private information while testing.
steps: Select Research, then Import (or Import PDF on an empty viewer) and choose a local .pdf.
Choose any previously imported PDF in Source document. Sources belong to the notebook, not just the page.
Navigate with Previous page, Next page or the PDF page field. The number is the physical page, starting at 1.
Use Zoom out / Zoom in. The initial zoom fits the pane width; there is no reset-to-fit button.
Optionally enter a Printed page number. It is a citation reference only and is not mapped automatically.
sections.expected: The PDF renders beside your notes. Scanned PDFs without a text layer have no extracted text, and this build does not perform OCR.

subsections.heading: Capture text and create Q&A
steps: Edit Selected PDF text down to the passage you need, or type or paste your own. It is pre-filled with the whole page's extracted text.
Focus a control inside the note that should receive it, then select Capture text.
Check the new source text block and its Source document · PDF p. … link.
For a Q&A, put the question wording in Selected PDF text and select Create Q&A. A new note is created with a sourced question and a linked blank answer.
subsections.callout: There is no selectable text layer over the PDF. Dragging across the page captures a rectangular image, not words. Changing the page or zoom refills the text field, so finish a text capture first.

subsections.heading: Capture a region and return to its source
steps: Focus the receiving note. On the PDF page, press at the upper-left of the region, drag down and right, then release. Use more than a few pixels.
A screenshot block appears immediately. There is no confirm step. If it is wrong, move the block to Trash and try again.
While in Research, select Source document · PDF p. …, Actions → View source, or Inspector → View source provenance to jump back.
Region capture keeps its bounds and page, but not the printed-page field.
subsections.callout: Jumping to a source from Write can miss the page change while the viewer loads. If so, click the link again after Research opens.

subsections.heading: Make room for reading or writing
steps: Use Collapse notebook sidebar and Expand notebook sidebar in the top toolbar.
In Research, drag the vertical separator to resize the source and notes panes.
Switch between Write and Research at any time. Switching unmounts the viewer, so recheck the PDF, page and capture text afterwards.

sections.title: Attach files, images and audio
steps: In Research, click the Attach media upload icon and choose Attach image, Attach screenshot, Attach audio or Attach file.
Choose a local file. It is copied into managed storage and added to the active note (or the first note). Cancelling changes nothing.
In Write, images can also be added from the command menu with /image.
Check the preview, the audio player, or Download attached file on file blocks.
sections.expected: Attach screenshot imports an existing image; it does not capture your desktop. Use PDF region capture for a PDF screenshot. If a preview stays on Loading image…, open diagnostics → Scan assets.

subsections.heading: Start and stop a recording
steps: In the desired note, select Record audio. Grant microphone access if asked. A working input device is required.
The button becomes Stop recording and a red Recording indicator with level bars appears.
Muted or disconnected devices are reported as Microphone muted or Microphone disconnected.
Select Stop recording and wait for the audio block. A WAV file is saved locally.
Check playback before transcribing.
subsections.callout: Always stop recording before switching pages, modes or closing the app. Leaving a recording note can discard the live recording unsaved.

sections.title: Set up and use transcription
sections.intro: Local transcription needs both a downloaded Whisper model and the packaged whisper.cpp runtime. A model alone cannot repair a missing runtime.

subsections.heading: Manage Local Whisper models
steps: Open Application menu → settings → Transcription. Models: Tiny, Base, Small, Medium and Large-v3, all multilingual.
Select Download on a model. Tiny is the smallest and a good first test. Downloads come from Hugging Face and need internet and disk space; audio stays local when transcribed.
Watch the progress bar. Cancel stops it, and Retry appears after a failure.
When Installed appears, choose Use as default. The default shows a disabled Default button.
To remove a model, first set another model as default, then select Remove on the non-default one and confirm.

subsections.heading: Request a transcript
steps: Return with Back to workspace. In an audio block choose Local Whisper or OpenRouter as the Transcription provider.
Pick Detect language automatically or a Language hint. It is a hint, not a translation control.
Select Transcribe. Local runs appear as queued/running jobs and show a percentage when available.
On completion the transcript text appears below the controls. The original audio stays attached.
On error, read the top alert and the jobs error, then check diagnostics. Retry failed local jobs after fixing the cause.
subsections.callout: If Local Whisper reports that the bundled sidecar is missing, you need a package that includes the Whisper runtime. There is no transcript history or transcript editor in this build.

subsections.heading: OpenRouter credentials and privacy
steps: In settings → Transcription enter your key under API key and select Save key.
Once saved, the controls become Replace API key and Remove key. The saved key is never shown.
In an audio block choose OpenRouter and press Transcribe only when you intend the external upload.
subsections.callout: OpenRouter sends the audio to an external service and usage may incur charges. There is no in-app pricing page, cloud model selector or cloud cancel button.

sections.title: Search what is actually indexed
steps: Click the top toolbar search button or press Ctrl + K (Cmd + K on macOS).
Type a word. Results update as you type.
Select a result to open its page. Notebook-title results open the first page. There is no guaranteed scroll-to-block highlight.
Press Escape to close without choosing.
bullets: Searches active notebook, page and note titles plus stored block data.
The query is split into word-like terms matched by prefix; all terms must match. Up to 100 ranked results.
It is not natural-language Q&A, exact-phrase search, full PDF search, OCR, or a search of attachment bytes.
PDF text becomes searchable once captured as block text.
The sidebar Search notes… field is a placeholder with no filtering. Use the top toolbar search.
Trash content is excluded from the index.

subsections.heading: Export a notebook, page or active note
steps: Save edits and open the page. If exporting Active note, focus a control in that note first.
Open Page actions → Export page.
Choose a Scope: Notebook, Current page or Active note.
Select a format button: markdown, pdf, lossless json or ai context.
Choose a destination folder and wait for the dialog to close. A new dated subfolder is created.

head: Format
File
What to expect
rows: Readable text with relative links to copied media.
Printable text and images. Audio and files appear as asset descriptions.
Versioned structured archive including relations, transcripts and captured sources.
Markdown with labels like [SOURCE] and [COMMENTARY]. Nothing is sent to an AI service.

subsections.callout: Every export folder also contains manifest.json and assets/. Keep the whole folder. Relationships outside the selected scope are excluded, so a narrow scope is not a full archive.

subsections.heading: Import a lossless archive
steps: Keep the .json file together with its sibling assets/ folder. Use the archive file, not manifest.json.
Open Application menu → Import backup and choose notebook.lossless.v1.json. Structure and checksums are validated first.
Relaunch the app if the new notebook does not appear in the sidebar.
Open the imported copy and verify source links and attachments.
subsections.callout: Import creates a new notebook copy with new identifiers and never overwrites. Importing twice makes two copies. Markdown, PDF and AI-context exports cannot be imported.

subsections.heading: Back up the whole library
steps: Stop any recording. Choose a destination outside the active library with enough free space.
Select Application menu → Back up library, or settings → Maintenance → Back up library.
Open jobs and wait for the backup job to show completed.
Keep database.sqlite, assets/, manifest.json and RECOVERY.md together, ideally with a second copy on another disk.
subsections.callout: A closed folder picker does not prove the backup finished. The backup does not include provider configuration, downloaded models or the library pointer.

subsections.heading: Recover a library backup
steps: There is no recovery button, and Import backup is not the path for a library backup. Ask the maintainer if you are unsure.
Record your Active library path, then close the app completely.
Preserve the entire current library in a separate recovery folder, including database sidecars.
Verify the asset SHA-256 hashes in manifest.json using RECOVERY.md.
Place the backup's database.sqlite and assets/ together in the active library location. Make sure stale database.sqlite-wal and -shm files are not left beside it.
If the library was relocated, restore to the path its pointer actually selects.
Relaunch the same build and verify notebook counts, text, source links, audio and files.

subsections.heading: Appearance and density
steps: Open Application menu → settings → General.
Choose Appearance: Use system setting, Light or Dark.
Choose Layout density: Default or Compact. Changes apply immediately without a restart.

subsections.heading: Relocate the library
steps: Make a library backup, save edits and stop recording first.
Open settings → Library & Storage and note the Active library path and sizes.
Select Move library… and choose a parent folder. The app copies and verifies the data into a new folder.
Wait for Move verified. Restart the application to activate the new library.
Relaunch and confirm the new Active library path and your content.
When satisfied and backed up, choose Remove original and confirm. This permanently deletes the retained original.
subsections.callout: Activation only happens after a restart. Avoid new edits between a verified move and the restart.

subsections.heading: Jobs: progress, cancel and retry
steps: Open Application menu → jobs, or settings → Maintenance.
Statuses are queued, running, succeeded, failed and cancelled.
Cancel a queued or running job. It may wait for a checkpoint.
Fix the cause of a failed job and select Retry. A new attempt is created and the old row stays.
subsections.callout: Local transcription, model downloads, backups and library moves use jobs. Restarting during a running job marks it interrupted.

subsections.heading: Diagnostics and asset scans
steps: Open Application menu → diagnostics. Filter by process, severity or category.
Expand an error and select Show full detail to read its message, context and stack.
Select Export diagnostics and choose a folder. Review the text for local paths before sharing.
Select Scan assets (or settings → Maintenance → Scan active notebook assets) to count missing, unreferenced and untracked files.
subsections.callout: Scans report only. They never delete or repair assets, and Export diagnostics does not submit feedback. Do not delete unreferenced files blindly.

sections.title: Trash and destructive actions
sections.intro: Test with disposable material and make a backup before any permanent deletion. Trash is local and has no timed auto-delete.
steps: Block: Actions → Move to trash, or Inspector → Move to trash.
Page: Page actions → Move page to trash. Its notes and blocks go too.
Notebook: the small trash icon beside its sidebar title. There is no confirmation for these recoverable moves.
Open Application menu → trash, find the item by title, type and date, and select Restore. Restoring a parent restores everything removed with it.
Select Delete only when the item is no longer needed.
sections.callout: Delete is permanent and has no second confirmation in this build. There is no Empty Trash and no direct note-delete control.

head: Shortcut
Action
rows: Add a note to the current page
Move the focused text block within its note

faq.a: Keep the exact message, version and package name. Preserve the library and never delete the database.
Leave the field, check the top alert, and reopen the page.

faq.q: Capture landed in the wrong note
faq.a: Focus a control inside the intended note before each capture, then trash the mistaken block.
Use the Selected PDF text field. Dragging the canvas captures an image region.
Finish the capture before changing page or zoom, which refill the field.

faq.q: Source link opens the wrong page
faq.a: Click it again once the viewer has loaded, or pick the source and page manually.
It may be scanned. This build has no OCR, so use an external OCR tool first.
Check microphone permission and the connected input, and use Record audio, not /audio.
Always press Stop recording before navigating away.

faq.q: Local transcription reports a missing sidecar
faq.a: Get a package that includes the Whisper runtime. Downloading a model alone is not enough.
Check network, disk space and jobs. Cancel, fix the cause, then retry.

faq.q: Import finished but no notebook appears
faq.a: Relaunch to refresh the sidebar and confirm you chose the .lossless.v1.json file with its assets.
Check destination permissions, disk space, asset scan and diagnostics. A partial folder is not a verified backup.
Wait for Move verified, restart, then check Active library.

sections.title: Guided first session
sections.intro: Use a disposable library, a non-private PDF, a small image and, optionally, a microphone. Plan about 20 to 30 minutes, not counting downloads.
steps: Create Learning research, rename its first page Reading and reasoning, and add a note.
Add a text block (research aim), a commentary and a question. Leave each field to save.
Use Add answer on the question and confirm responds to in the Inspector.
Duplicate a block, reorder it with the menu and Alt + ↑/↓, trash it, then restore it.
Create Practice captures, add a note, open Research and import your PDF.
Trim the extracted text to a passage and select Capture text. Create a Q&A note and capture a small region.
Click the source link while in Research and confirm the right page. Resize the divider and toggle the sidebar.
Attach an image and a file. Record a short clip and stop it before navigating.
Check transcription setup. Treat an unavailable runtime or model as blocked, not as success.
Search for a saved word. Export the page as Markdown and PDF, and the notebook as lossless JSON.
Import the lossless archive as a new copy and relaunch. Make a whole-library backup and confirm the job completed.
Reopen the app and verify your content. Export diagnostics if anything failed.

sections.title: Tester feedback template
sections.intro: Research Notebook does not submit feedback automatically. Copy this into your team's issue tracker or message.
